title: Questioning the summary statement
coreMove: Make the summary line specific, level-accurate, and structurally faithful to the conclusions beneath it.
sourcePressure: Chapter 9 tests the summary statement: stating action effects, making wording specific, distinguishing levels of action, drawing inference from conclusions, finding structural similarity, and visualizing relationships.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Writing a polished headline that sounds strategic while overclaiming, underclaiming, or blurring what the lower points prove.

sourceAnchors.name: effect of actions
sourceAnchors.detail: the Chapter 9 heading map supports testing whether the summary statement states the effect of actions
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A real summary names the effect the actions jointly create, not just the activity they keep busy with.

sourceAnchors.name: visualize the relationships
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar says visualization of relationships is a supported aid for checking the summary line
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: When the relationships are sketched, a vague top line has fewer places to hide.

hook: A polished heading pretends the structure underneath is solved
opening with an abstract definition of clarity
starting with a generic frustrated professional staring at a blank document
counterintuition: The point is not polish; the point is discipline
clarity is not about writing less; it is about thinking better
structure sounds rigid but actually creates freedom
tryThisNow: Ask what the reader needs to know next
ask yourself what the point is
examples: manager fixes a team memo with colored markers
same protagonist revises a deck under meeting pressure
same scene as prior chapter with swapped document type

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective recognition, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm through a direct second-person passage, a short research/source aside, a reader question, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional pharmacy chain summarizing medication-adherence pilots
exampleSpecs.stakes: executives may fund scattered activities unless the summary names the shared patient effect
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hugo changes improve adherence programs to reduce missed refills in high-risk patients after checking that each pilot supports that effect.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Orange prescription labels line the edge of Hugo's conference table.

exampleSpecs.domain: a shipping insurer summarizing three loss-prevention actions
exampleSpecs.audience: claims and underwriting teams needing level control
exampleSpecs.stakes: a vague loss prevention heading will hide which action affects frequency and which affects severity
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chloé asks what effect all three actions actually share, then splits severity-reduction actions from frequency-reduction actions before writing two summary lines.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Which loss did these actions prevent: more claims, or worse claims?

exampleSpecs.domain: a university athletics director reporting academic-support changes
exampleSpecs.stakes: the provost will dismiss the plan if the summary says support students without naming the effect
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Matthew rewrites expand tutoring into raise first-year eligibility retention after checking that advising, tutoring, and progress alerts all point there.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Matthew one retention table to stop calling the actions the result.

exampleSpecs.domain: a textile factory quality team summarizing defect-reduction work
exampleSpecs.stakes: plant leaders need to know whether the work reduces rework time, customer returns, or scrap
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Cleaner quality process says nothing," Anke says, then visualizes inspection, calibration, and packing relationships until the common effect is fewer customer returns.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Cleaner quality process says nothing," Anke says beside a bolt of rejected fabric.

exampleSpecs.domain: a civic-data team naming the result of permit-processing changes
exampleSpecs.stakes: leaders will overclaim transformation if the changes only reduce one queue bottleneck
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Devon draw the permit stages, locate where each action acts, and lower the summary from citywide modernization to two-day reduction in intake review.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are looking at a permit-flow sketch with one thick red bottleneck.

exampleSpecs.domain: a specialty coffee roaster summarizing wholesale account changes
exampleSpecs.audience: small-business managers connecting actions to effects
exampleSpecs.stakes: the owner may expand discounts when the evidence supports retention through delivery reliability
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 2:15 p.m., Frida replaces strengthen wholesale with reduce account churn by improving delivery reliability, then deletes one pricing point that does not fit.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 2:15 p.m., Frida places three returned coffee bags beside the churn report.

skillTargets: turn activity labels into effect statements
infer a top line without leaping beyond support
use structural similarity to test whether one summary can cover the group

tryThisNowSpec: Take one heading and add the words so that after it. If you cannot name the effect, the summary is probably activity, not conclusion.
